rows.note: Use 喊 as the all-purpose everyday verb for crying or shouting; context makes the meaning clear.

example.english: The child started to cry immediately after falling.
example.jyutping: sai3 lou6 zai2 dit3 can1 zik1 hak1 haam3

rows.note: Use 流眼淚 when you specifically mean that tears are coming out, rather than simply crying or shouting.

example.english: The onion was so pungent that it made me cry.
example.jyutping: ngo5 bei2 joeng4 cung1 laat6 dou3 lau4 ngaan5 leoi6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for an individual shout or scream, rather than crying or a general uproar.

example.english: They suddenly gave a loud cry.
example.jyutping: keoi5 dat6 jin4 daai6 haam3 jat1 seng1

rows.note: Use this for a bout of crying, especially when describing someone having a good cry.

example.english: I had a good cry last night, and felt much better afterward.
example.traditional: 琴晚我有一輪喊，喊完個人舒服晒。
example.jyutping: kam4 maan5 ngo5 jau5 jat1 leon4 haam3 haam3 jyun4 go3 jan4 syu1 fuk6 saai3

rows.note: Use this for the noise or clamour of a general uproar, not for one person’s shout.

example.english: The clamour downstairs was a loud cry that kept me awake.
example.traditional: 樓下傳嚟一片嘈吵聲，搞到我瞓唔着。
example.jyutping: lau4 haa6 cyun4 lei4 jat1 pin3 cou4 caau2 sing1 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use this specifically for an urgent cry or call for help.

example.english: I heard someone let out a cry for help in the corridor.
example.traditional: 我喺走廊聽到有人發出求救聲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 zau2 long4 teng1 dou2 jau5 jan4 faat3 ceot1 kau4 gau3 sing1
